note: THE CENSUS YELLOW ALARM CANNOT SEE A SLOW CENSUS THAT QUEUED, AND COUNTS A FAILED ONE AS SUCCESSFUL. Measured, not inferred. docs/timings.md HAS NO RETURN-CODE COLUMN AT ALL -- its eleven fields are when, label, wall_s, user_s, sys_s, cpu_ratio, waited_s, commit, branch, host, cores. scripts/timed.sh only ECHOES the rc to stderr and returns it; the printf that writes the ledger row never includes it, and it runs BEFORE the return, so a FAILED run still lands a row. But cli/tests/suite/census_duration.rs parse_successful_census_rows keeps a row when parts index 7 equals zero and calls that SUCCESSFUL -- and index 7 is waited_s, the seconds spent waiting for the shared claim. Two consequences, both live. FIRST, A SUCCESSFUL CENSUS THAT QUEUED IS DROPPED: of 45 census rows, 2 are excluded, and one of them is 2026-08-24T12:05:18Z at 904.554 s, which is OVER the 900 s alarm threshold. A yellow run invisible to the yellow alarm, solely because it waited 683 s for the lock. That is the exact class of run the alarm exists to force a look at, and queueing is now the NORMAL state since every expensive job takes one serial claim. SECOND, A FAILED CENSUS THAT DID NOT WAIT READS AS SUCCESSFUL, because there is no rc to filter on and waited_s is zero. WHY IT LOOKS RIGHT: the function name says successful, its doc comment says successful, and the predicate is a bare index into a split. Nothing in the file names the column, so the reader supplies the meaning. The neighbouring helper latest_by_timestamp carries a careful comment about NOT using rows.last because the file is not reliably ordered -- real care, one line above a filter keyed on the wrong field entirely. FOUND HOW: an implementer reported that a gate-commit run printed rc=2 while the ledger row read rc=0, which was itself a misreading -- it was reading waited_s as rc -- and chasing the misreading found the defect the misreading was accidentally describing. NOT FIXED HERE: campaign/the-escapement has a merge queued that just passed the mouth, and this is a pre-existing defect in a different file; fixing it now would cost the queue slot for no safety gain. Filing as a follow-up. WHOEVER FIXES IT: adding an rc column to timed.sh changes the ledger schema every reader parses by index, so the cheap correct fix is probably to make the predicate honest about what it can actually know rather than to widen the schema.
